entry.title: 3Speak Encoder: big update for node operators 🎬

link.title: 3Speak Encoder: big update for node operators 🎬

entry.content:
Greetings and Salutations Hiveans! 👋 Over the last few days we've shipped the biggest batch of changes the 3Speak encoder has had in a while: **20 updates** covering installation, the dashboard, uploads and reliability. If you run an encoder for the community, this post is for you. There's a short **"How to upgrade"** section at the end. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mantequilla-soft/23wWwQmgLtrubjegAvbwjFrqsT9xTAqgeUaL5ign8R6bfNrJ4RAky1xtQwpZ56VDPYtSj.jpg) --- ## 🚀 Installing is now one line New operators can get going with a single command: **Linux / Mac** ``` curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/main/install.sh | bash ``` **Windows (PowerShell)** ``` iwr -useb https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/main/install.ps1 | iex ``` The installer works out what's missing and installs it: Git, Node.js, FFmpeg and IPFS. Then it downloads the encoder, sets it up from a few questions and checks that everything works before it finishes. Every change is tested by installing on fresh Windows, Mac and Linux machines (Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora and Arch). What got fixed along the way: - **Windows: "FFmpeg not found" is gone.** The old installer needed an administrator window. Without one it failed quietly and still said everything was fine. It now uses winget, which comes with Windows 10 and 11 and needs no admin rights. It checks that FFmpeg actually runs and saves its location, so the encoder always finds it. - **Mac:** works out of the box on Apple Silicon Macs. - **Linux:** Fedora and Arch are supported, and older systems like Ubuntu 22.04 get a recent Node.js automatically. - **Start automatically (optional):** the installer can make IPFS and the encoder start whenever the computer boots (Linux) or you log in (Mac, Windows). No more forgetting to restart your node after a reboot. - **New `npm run doctor` command:** checks Node.js, FFmpeg and IPFS and tells you in plain words what's missing. If something's off, run this first. ⚠️ **Important for people who installed a while ago:** an old installer option ("Gateway mode") set up encoders that **never received any jobs**. If your encoder has sat idle for a long time, that may be why. The encoder now warns at startup with `No job source enabled`. The fix is three lines in your `.env`: ``` EMBED_SYSTEM_ENABLED=true EMBED_SYSTEM_MODE=community EMBED_GATEWAY_URL=https://embed.3speak.tv ``` --- ## 🖥️ A brand new dashboard ![Screenshot 2026-10-31 at 1.35.27 PM.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/mantequilla-soft/23swe5kv3u8AuRLjDoSN95hkNEZ57cbkw4gzbx2qeWRdCVPVrRUg8UofrzdwjZCMgyR7A.png) The local dashboard at `http://localhost:3001` got a full redesign, inspired by the tiling-desktop look of Tokyo Night colours theme. - **Easier to read at a glance:** the current job, encoder health, recent jobs, anything that needs your attention, and the live log. - **Accurate status:** the dashboard used to show "Offline" while the encoder was busy and perfectly fine. It now tells apart *Encoding*, *Not responding* (frozen), *Unreachable* (stopped, or the port is blocked) and *Offline* (shutting down). - **Health numbers:** how responsive the encoder process is, and how long it's been up. - **Install it as an app:** on your phone or computer, the dashboard can be installed like an app with its own icon. Use **Install app** in the top bar in Chrome, Edge or Android, or **Add to Home Screen** in Safari. This needs the dashboard on HTTPS, so it's for operators who reach their node through a domain name. - **Optional password and safer defaults:** you can now set a dashboard password, or limit the dashboard to your own machine. It also blocks a class of attacks where another website open in your browser tries to control your encoder. --- ## 🔄 Updates and versions - **Know when you're behind:** the dashboard shows which version you run and how many updates you're missing, with a link to what changed. **Check for updates** checks right away. - **One-click updates (optional):** turn it on with `SELF_UPDATE_ENABLED=true` and an `UPDATE_PASSWORD`, and you can update from the dashboard. The encoder finishes its current jobs first, updates, and restarts itself. If anything goes wrong, it rolls back to the version that was working. It's off by default, works on git installs (not Docker), and needs the encoder started with the included start script, which the installer's shortcuts use. - **No more half-updated nodes:** if the encoder can't build after an update (most often because files belong to another user after a `sudo` command), it now stops with a clear message instead of starting on a mix of old and new code. - **Your version, visible to 3Speak:** encoders now report which version they run and how far behind they are, so we can see at a glance who needs to update and reach out. It's only the version: no personal data, and nothing changes about the jobs you get. --- ## 📦 Uploads: simpler and more honest - **Uploads go to 3Speak's hotnodes only.** The old upload path to the "supernode" has been removed for good. - **When an upload fails:** by default the job is reported as failed, so 3Speak knows and can give it to another encoder. Before, the encoder fell back to the old supernode. - **Optional local backup (`ENABLE_LOCAL_FALLBACK=true`):** if the upload fails, your node keeps the video on its own IPFS node and keeps trying to move it to a hotnode in the background. The video keeps the same address, so viewers never notice. Only recommended for operators with fast and reliable internet connections. - **See where every backed-up video stands:** the dashboard's storage section lists each one as *waiting to move*, *moved*, *removed* or *deleted*, with dates and the video's owner and link. One click checks the video is reachable before you do anything by hand. --- ## 🛠️ Under the hood - **FFmpeg 8 support:** the encoder failed to start on FFmpeg 8 and newer (`Input format lavfi is not available`). Fixed. - **Docker:** the production Docker image and compose file wouldn't build or run. Both are fixed; the compose file runs the encoder together with its own IPFS node. - **Steadier startup:** the encoder waits up to 90 seconds for IPFS instead of giving up at once, which matters when both start together at boot. - **Automatic tests:** every change now runs through automatic tests on Linux and Windows, plus the full install on Windows, Mac and several Linux distributions. - **Documentation:** the README and install guides have been rewritten to match how things work today. --- ## ✅ How to upgrade **Requirement:** Node.js **20 or newer**. Check with `node -v`. If you have 18 or older, update Node.js first from https://nodejs.org (the LTS version), or let the installer do it. **Option A: you installed with git (most operators)** In your encoder folder (usually `~/3speak-encoder`, or `C:\Users\\3speak-encoder` on Windows): ``` git pull npm ci npm run doctor ``` Then restart the encoder the way you normally start it. Your settings and your encoder identity stay as they are. **Option B: run the installer again** Run the one-line command from the top of this post. It keeps your encoder identity and saves your old settings as `.env.bak`. If you had changed extra settings (a dashboard password, local backup, and so on), copy them back from `.env.bak` into `.env`. **Option C: Docker** ``` git pull GIT_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD) docker compose -f docker-compose.production.yml up -d --build ``` **Good to know after upgrading:** - **Opening the dashboard by a name** (like `encoder.mydomain.com` instead of an IP address)? Add that name to `.env` as `DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_HOSTS=encoder.mydomain.com` and restart. Otherwise the dashboard answers "Host not allowed". This is part of the new protection against malicious websites. - **Don't use `sudo`** for `git pull`, `npm` or starting the encoder. It leaves files the encoder can't update later. If you did in the past, fix it once on Linux or Mac with `sudo chown -R $(whoami): .` in the encoder folder. - **Something not working?** Run `npm run doctor` first. It points at the problem in plain words. --- Thanks to everyone running an encoder: you're the ones keeping 3Speak videos flowing. 🙌 If you hit a problem, open an issue on [GitHub](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/issues) or find us on Discord.
[![Mantequilla Soft](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSCTXSSRQ4R5Xq2pGTTiiMuSsTcJYAy1ozfkb35M7jVzB/mantequilla-soft-logo.png)](https://www.mantequilla-soft.com) **[GitHub](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft) · [Website](https://www.mantequilla-soft.com) · [Snapie](https://snapie.io) · [3Speak](https://3speak.tv)**
</div> *— The Mantequilla Soft team*</div>
Source: 3Speak Encoder: big update for node operators 🎬 by @mantequilla-soft

entry.title: Exchange node in four lines (Hive 1.28.8)
entry.content:
How many commands does it take to run a Hive node for an exchange? Four. One of them is `cd`, and the last one is for watching the logs while you drink your coffee ;-) Remember [Hive Node Setup for the Smart, the Dumb, and the Lazy](/@gtg/hive-node-setup-for-the-smart-the-dumb-and-the-lazy)? This one is for the lazy. ## No scripts, one compose file We were asked for a "cloud-native" way to run a node: no helper scripts, just one declarative file. Hive 1.28.8 has exactly that: [`docker/exchange`](https://github.com/openhive-network/hive/tree/1.28.8/docker/exchange), a Docker Compose setup for an exchange node. I serve a copy of it at https://gtg.openhive.network/get/exchange/ - slightly modified from upstream: it tracks the accounts I chose to support, so it matches my exchange snapshot, and it keeps the block log and the snapshot in plain folders next to the compose file.
![Cyberpunk-Hive-chan.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTZJyTj2iXDnJBRZ8ZpEN4FeGZMwm65H1hvGKvrSU1Muv/Cyberpunk-Hive-chan.png)Cyberpunk Hive chan, generated by AI during HiveFest 2026
## What's in the box ``` hive-exchange-1.28.8 ├── .env <- your settings: ports, BLOCK_LOG_DIR, SNAPSHOT_URL ├── compose.yml <- the node itself, nothing to edit ├── config.ini <- hived options and the tracked accounts ├── README.md ├── blockchain <- your block_log, or block_log_part.* files └── snapshot <- the unpacked snapshot (downloaded here if empty) ``` **You have a block log?** If you had a Hive node running recently, you probably do. It's preferred and recommended to re-use it. Blocks never change. That's the whole point. Put it into `blockchain`: one big `block_log` file or a set of `block_log_part.*` files, both work. Or keep it where it is and point `BLOCK_LOG_DIR` in `.env` to it. **No block log?** Leave `blockchain` empty. The node then runs pruned (see below). The snapshot takes care of itself: if `snapshot` is empty, the node downloads my exchange snapshot (6.3 GB) into it. Already have it unpacked? Put it there. ## The four lines ``` wget -qO- https://gtg.openhive.network/get/exchange/hive-exchange-1.28.8.tgz | tar xz cd hive-exchange-1.28.8 docker compose up -d docker compose logs -f hived ``` Unpack it on the disk where the block log is (or will be). If your block log stays where it is, add one line before `docker compose up -d`: ``` echo BLOCK_LOG_DIR=/path/to/your/blockchain >> .env ``` ~~Four lines~~ Five lines. The coffee is still the last one. The node loads the snapshot, replays your block log from the snapshot's block on, and syncs the rest from the network. Without a block log, it does the same minus the replay. Minutes, not even hours. When the log says `entering live mode`, press Ctrl+C. That stops the log, not the node. `docker compose ps` shows the node as `healthy` once it has caught up.
![Exchange node in five lines](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPCCebURJ18jqqpNJ2XoBQPHe947Z1xWmzU3gRSh7NTNW/exchange-node-block-log.gif)The real run with a block log, sped up
The log stopped at the same block for minutes? > _Have you tried turning it off and on again?_ > - Roy, The IT Crowd ``` docker compose down && docker compose up -d ``` ## Your block log, three rules - Stop your old node first. - hived in the container runs as UID 1000, so it has to be able to write there: `sudo chown -R 1000 blockchain` (or your `BLOCK_LOG_DIR`). - Your block log has to be at least as new as the snapshot: it must contain the block the snapshot was made at. A node that was in sync until you stopped it is fine. An older one makes hived stop with "Chain state ... does not match block log", over and over. ## All blocks, or pruned? With a block log, the node has all blocks: either in one big file (`block-log-split = -1`) or in parts of a million blocks each (`block-log-split = 9999`, the hived default). `config.ini` says `-1`, and when the bundle finds `block_log_part.*` files it switches to `9999` for you. Want parts instead of one big file? Set `block-log-split = 9999` in `config.ini` and hived splits it on the next start. It keeps the original file, so you need the space twice until you delete it. Without a block log, the node is pruned: it runs with `block-log-split = 0` and keeps only the newest block. State is complete, and so is the account history of the accounts on the list. That is enough to follow your deposits. But `get_block` and `get_transaction` need all blocks. No block log of your own, but you want all blocks? Set this in `.env` before the first start: ``` BLOCK_LOG_URL=https://gtg.openhive.network/get/blockchain/block_log ``` The node then downloads the block log into `blockchain`, loads the snapshot, and replays only the blocks made after the snapshot. ## Is your account on the list? The snapshot has account history only for the accounts listed in `config.ini` (the `account-history-rocksdb-track-account-range` lines). On the list? You are done. Keep the list as it is. Not on the list? Then the snapshot cannot give you its history. Before the first start, add your account to `config.ini` and clear `SNAPSHOT_URL` in `.env`. With a block log the node replays all of it, with history for your account from the first block. That takes hours, not minutes. Without one, it syncs the whole chain from the P2P network, which takes even longer. Running an exchange that people actually use, and your account isn't on the list? Let me know, with a good reason, and it can be in the next snapshot. `SNAPSHOT_URL` points to `latest-1.28.8.tgz`, which is always my newest snapshot made with 1.28.8. ## The block log rule **Never download the block log twice.** Monolithic or split, keep it and reuse it for every replay and every upgrade. It is 587 GB today, and it does not get any smaller. That is what the `blockchain` folder is for. `docker compose down -v` removes the volumes, that is the state and the account history. The `blockchain` and `snapshot` folders stay. Plain `docker compose down` keeps everything. ## Bonus: asking the node The API listens on `127.0.0.1:8091` only. Keep it off the public internet. Where is the chain? ``` curl -s --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"database_api.get_dynamic_global_properties","id":1}' http://127.0.0.1:8091/ ``` Look for `head_block_number` and `last_irreversible_block_num`. The last 10 operations of an account. Let's take `binance-hot2`, one of Binance's accounts on the list: ``` curl -s --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"account_history_api.get_account_history","params":{"account":"binance-hot2","start":-1,"limit":10},"id":1}' http://127.0.0.1:8091/ ``` Each entry has the operation, its `block` and its `trx_id`. By default you get only operations from irreversible blocks, so everything you see there is final. This one works on a pruned node too. Did a transaction make it? Ask with its `trx_id`: ``` curl -s --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"account_history_api.get_transaction","params":{"id":"TRX_ID"},"id":1}' http://127.0.0.1:8091/ ``` If you get the transaction back, it is in an irreversible block. Until then the answer is "Unknown Transaction", and thanks to OBI that usually lasts only seconds. It needs all blocks, and it knows the transactions of the accounts on the list. And a block: ``` curl -s --data '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"block_api.get_block","params":{"block_num":BLOCK_NUM},"id":1}' http://127.0.0.1:8091/ ``` That needs all blocks too. A pruned node answers "has been pruned" for everything but the newest one. For deposits, account history is the better tool anyway: it also shows virtual operations, like recurrent transfers or transfers from savings, which you will not find in any block. It's an exchange node, but other nodes run almost the same way: a seed node, a witness node, a personal wallet node, a broadcaster, or a basic API node for your simple bots. Same compose file, a different `config.ini`, and most likely the same snapshot. hived only warns that the snapshot has more plugins than it needs. Seed and API nodes need all the blocks, though, so bring your block log.
Source: Exchange node in four lines (Hive 1.28.8) by @gtg

entry.title: Hive Dev Proposal #3
entry.content:
<div class="hive-post-embed" data-hive-author="hdev" data-hive-permlink="hive-dev-proposal-3"> <div id="content-hdev-hive-dev-proposal-3" class="hive-post-embed__content" data-hive-render-target="true">Since mid-2024, our team has been building Hive tools in the HAF ecosystem, working alongside @blocktrades and the core development team. This is our third Hive Dev proposal, and we want to start with a big thank you to everyone who supported the first two.
![Hive logo above the words "Dev Proposal #3", with three developers at a laptop, an analytics dashboard and mobile apps](https://usermedia.actifit.io/MVU1N298R4N5J3DDRT8S3NYZDYVWZD)
Proposal #2 was funded for only about the second half of its term. During that period, 25 people contributed through our work, and we merged **434 merge requests** across 10 Hive repositories and shipped:
- **Two new HAF apps:** **haf\_stats** (network analytics) and **haf\_fyp** (a personalised For You feed), both now standard modules in the latest haf\_api\_node release. **PeakD serves haf\_fyp's ranking** to its readers. - **hivescan.info as an analytics hub:** a dashboard you arrange yourself, sign-in with Keychain and HiveSigner, account analytics with a delegation map, a **DHF Governance Hub**, and network, RC and governance reports in 12 languages. - **New endpoints and fixes in Hive's core backends:** Balance Tracker, HAF Block Explorer, Hivemind, HiveSense and HAF, including rebuilt escrow tracking, corrected witness vote counts, and a Hivemind bug that silently skipped blocks, which we found and diagnosed on our node. - **Two public HAF API nodes** that we run, carrying the full stack. - **Apps that bring people to Hive:** Waggle; HivePulse, now a Hive wallet with a Scam Shield, on Chrome and Firefox; Hive Runner; four apps, not yet launched, from our **summer developer cohort**; Actifit's on-chain challenges engine, **The Arena**, with redesigned Android and iOS apps; weekly contests that pay Hive writers in HIVE, run in our new Hdev Contests community; and **Vylor**, a finance app built this year and live on Google Play and the App Store.
Our ask is 275 HBD/day, about 34% less than our prior proposal's adjusted rate, after streamlining our developer allocation and infrastructure. Below is what we delivered, what comes next and what the ask pays for. Thank you for reading, and for helping us keep improving Hive.
## Summary
In the year of proposal #2 (2025-11-01 to 2026-10-28) the team merged **434 merge requests across 10 Hive GitLab repositories**. It also shipped two new HAF applications, **haf\_stats** and **haf\_fyp**, and both are standard modules in the latest haf\_api\_node release, 1.28.8. This proposal (#3) funds the next year: keeping those apps and the Block Explorer moving, and the new work listed under Upcoming work.
What the year delivered, at a glance:
- **haf\_stats**, a new HAF analytics app: 114 MRs, with network statistics, governance, RC and per-account endpoints feeding the Block Explorer's dashboards. - **haf\_fyp**, a new HAF app for a personalised For You feed: 112 MRs. It is live: PeakD, Waggle and HivePulse serve its ranking, and Denser plans to. - **Block Explorer UI** ([hivescan.info](https://hivescan.info)): 148 MRs, adding a modular dashboard, sign-in with Keychain and HiveSigner, a full analytics and reporting section, and per-account analytics that complete roadmap items 2 and 5. - **Backend work** in Balance Tracker, HAF Block Explorer, HAF, Hivemind, HiveSense and haf\_api\_node: 60 MRs. - **Waggle**, a For You feed front end, the Hive Runner game and the **HivePulse** browser extension and wallet, on GitHub; four Hive apps in development from our summer cohort of Hive developers; Actifit's new on-chain challenges engine (The Arena), its apps and site; and Vylor, a personal finance app that works with Hive, live on Google Play and the App Store. In all, 3,192 commits on GitHub, cohort developers and contributors included. - **Two public HAF API nodes** we run: testapi.hivescan.info and hiveapi.actifit.io.
### Roadmap from proposal #2
| # | Item | Status | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1 | Customizable modular dashboard | Done | [block\_explorer\_ui#673](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/block_explorer_ui/-/issues/673), then templates and synced workspaces | | 2 | Interactive financial sunburst | Done: Financial Summary sunburst in the Account Analytics tab | [block\_explorer\_ui#653](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/block_explorer_ui/-/issues/653) | | 3 | User authentication | Done: Keychain and HiveSigner sign-in | [block\_explorer\_ui#672](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/block_explorer_ui/-/issues/672) | | 4 | RC footprint and DApp usage dashboard | Done, now priced from each transaction's recorded RC | [haf\_stats](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_stats), [block\_explorer\_ui#654](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/block_explorer_ui/-/issues/654) | | 5 | Influence and delegation map | Done: Influence & Delegation Map in the Account Analytics tab | [block\_explorer\_ui#655](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/block_explorer_ui/-/issues/655) | | 6 | Hive reporting dashboard | Done: dashboard widgets plus reports pages | [hivescan.info](https://hivescan.info) | | 7 | HAF backend endpoints (DAU, TVL, RC footprint, financial, RC delegations) | Done | haf\_stats, balance\_tracker, haf | | 9 | HAF\_FYP | Done and live | [haf\_fyp](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_fyp) | | 8 | HAF\_CHAT | Not started this year | — |
## Delivered work, by project
Everything below is public. Each project links to its merged MRs, and most features can be tried on [hivescan.info](https://hivescan.info) or on our API node [testapi.hivescan.info](https://testapi.hivescan.info).
| Project | Merged MRs | Who | | --- | --- | --- | | [block\_explorer\_ui](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/block_explorer_ui/-/merge_requests?scope=all&state=merged) | 148 | delrifai 121, mcfarhat 27 | | [haf\_stats](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_stats/-/merge_requests?scope=all&state=merged) | 114 | mcfarhat 86, mahdi 28 | | [haf\_fyp](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_fyp/-/merge_requests?scope=all&state=merged) | 112 | mcfarhat 104, mahdi 8 | | [haf\_block\_explorer](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_block_explorer/-/merge_requests?scope=all&state=merged) | 24 | mzander 13, mahdi 10, mcfarhat 1 | | [balance\_tracker](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/balance_tracker/-/merge_requests?scope=all&state=merged) | 15 | mzander 8, mahdi 6, mcfarhat 1 | | [haf\_api\_node](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_api_node/-/merge_requests?scope=all&state=merged) | 7 | mcfarhat 7 | | [hivemind](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/hivemind/-/merge_requests?scope=all&state=merged) | 5 | mzander 4, mcfarhat 1 | | [haf](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf/-/merge_requests?scope=all&state=merged) | 4 | mzander 4 | | [healthchecker-component](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/healthchecker-component/-/merge_requests?scope=all&state=merged) | 3 | mcfarhat 3 | | [hivesense](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/hivesense/-/merge_requests?scope=all&state=merged) | 2 | mcfarhat 2 |
### haf\_stats — Hive network analytics (new HAF app)
A new HAF app that turns raw chain data into chart-ready network statistics and per-account metrics: activity, governance, Resource Credits and DApp usage. It is the data layer behind hivescan.info's analytics and reports. Because it ships in the standard HAF API node stack, any node operator can serve it and any front end can build on it. [Repository](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_stats).
- **Network statistics:** daily active users, vote stats, content volume, engagement, a top-accounts leaderboard, HP distribution and author retention and signup-cohort funnels. Values are checked against a real 5M-block replay. ([daily active users](https://testapi.hivescan.info/haf-stats-api/network/daily-active-users), [top accounts](https://testapi.hivescan.info/haf-stats-api/network/top-accounts)) - **Checked against Hivemind:** post counts match Hivemind exactly on all 3,864 days from 2016-03-24 to 2026-10-21, and comment counts stay within 2%. That gap came from a Hivemind sync issue we reported and the core team fixed on October 26, [hivemind#394](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/hivemind/-/issues/394). Two counting bugs found on the way, a double count and a ~19% over-report, were fixed first. ([the check](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_stats/-/merge_requests/124)) - **Governance:** stake concentration (Gini coefficient, top-1% and top-10% shares) and per-witness missed-block stats. ([influence concentration](https://testapi.hivescan.info/haf-stats-api/governance/influence-concentration)) - **Resource Credits:** network RC utilization, per-account RC footprint and a DApp footprint that maps custom\_json to named apps in 9 categories. It adds a per-event RC timeline for each account, and RC estimates calibrated against the node's own rc\_api (the old model priced a typical custom\_json about 3× too high). Since October, RC uses each transaction's **recorded cost** where the node has it. ([RC footprint](https://testapi.hivescan.info/haf-stats-api/account/actifit/rc-footprint)) - **Communities and social graph:** an account's activity per community (each reply traced up to its root post, checked against Hivemind on 120 real threads), its top partners for replies, votes, transfers, reblogs and follows, and a network-wide DApp usage leaderboard by app or category. These power hivescan.info's community, Sankey and DApp-usage reports. - **Account finances:** a per-account financial summary covering 15 operation types, incoming and outgoing. - **Performance:** a year of daily active users went from 7.8 s to 4.6 ms (~1,700× faster), a heavy account's RC footprint from ~104 s to ~4.3 s and the 365-day top-accounts query from ~22 s to 0.98 s. A nightly refresh's slowest read fell from 8.3 s to 2–4 ms, and the network DApp usage leaderboard from ~20 s to about 0.55 s. A full rebuild of account financial history went from tens of hours to 1–2 hours. All were measured on our node, testapi. - **Operations:** a safe install, upgrade and uninstall, tested in CI against the real installer; a version endpoint and a corrected sync status; a published image; and a published disk footprint for operators (about 125 GB on compressed ZFS). It also fixed a stall in which haf\_stats, waiting on Hivemind, could hold up Hivemind and its API on the whole node. It ships as a standard module in the latest release, 1.28.8, of the [haf\_api\_node](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_api_node) stack.
### haf\_fyp — personalised For You feed (new HAF app)
The open-source discovery engine promised as item 9 of proposal #2: a personalised For You feed computed from HAF data. Front ends get a ready-made feed in Hive bridge format, readers get posts picked for them, and a score explainer shows why each post was picked. [Repository](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_fyp).
- **Ranking:** recency, engagement, author credibility (stake and reputation) and semantic relevance from HiveSense embeddings, with a per-community diversity cap. New readers pick a few interests, so their first feed is never empty. Posts the reader or their community muted are left out. - **Ranking that works as designed:** only 0.31% of posts had a community recorded, so the community boost barely applied; it is now 21.35%, with a stronger boost for communities a reader subscribes to. New readers' interest profiles were never built for established communities, and readers who picked interests but never voted were never re-ranked, so their feeds sat 12–15 days old. All three are fixed. - **Fresh for people who read it:** a reader's feed used to be about 11 hours old on average, and up to 22. Readers who open their feed are now ranked first, and a read that arrived during a ranking pass no longer waits 12–16 minutes but about 2 s; in a test on our node, a stale feed was re-ranked 9 s after it was opened. ([MR](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_fyp/-/merge_requests/99)) - **API:** personalised and global feeds in Hive bridge format, a score explainer and an algorithm registry. A 20-post page is served in about 0.13–0.16 s end to end. Rendered posts are cached, so on the server a 20-post page takes 35 ms personalised (was 911 ms) and 12 ms global (was 345 ms). ([global feed](https://testapi.hivescan.info/haf-fyp-api/v1/fyp/global), [a personal feed](https://testapi.hivescan.info/haf-fyp-api/v1/fyp/feed/mcfarhat)) - **Telemetry:** front ends report impressions, opens and dwell time, and the app rolls them into daily metrics. It can also A/B test two ranking versions against each other. PeakD has sent these events since October 6: 322 from 18 accounts by October 15. - **Security:** changes to a reader's interests must be signed with their posting key, and delegated posting authority is accepted. Readers can opt out with a signed request; the same change fixed a bug that made saving interests fail for every reader on some installs. Rate limits apply per client, charged before a request is read when the node gateway identifies the caller. An opt-in setting stops forged reads from claiming ranking slots. - **Adoption:** **PeakD** serves haf\_fyp's ranking to its readers. From September 23 to October 15, 326 of 442 feed requests (74%) came from PeakD, for 105 accounts, on all 23 days. We measure this from request origins in our node's logs. Our own Waggle and HivePulse's For You tab run on it too, and Denser plans to adopt it. - **Operations:** one query had used about 98% of the app's CPU and starved the whole node: Block Explorer and Balance Tracker fell 43 blocks behind and returned errors. A partial index fixed it (load from ~5.7 to ~1.6) and both recovered. Node operators can now tune feed freshness: on our node a full re-ranking pass went from ~22 h to under 4 h. It also gained a /metrics health endpoint, a personalised fallback when HiveSense is down, HAF app locks, truthful health checks, install lanes tested against real HAF in CI and a published image. It ships as a standard module in the latest haf\_api\_node release, 1.28.8.
![Waggle screenshot](https://usermedia.actifit.io/MVU1H2L3LTJ01GN2UMRCJ33JHQTVK)
*Waggle, running on haf\_fyp, shows each reader why a post was picked: relevance, recency, engagement and credibility, plus a boost for communities they follow.*
### Block Explorer UI — hivescan.info
The explorer front end. This year it became an analytics hub for Hive: a dashboard you arrange yourself, sign-in with Keychain or HiveSigner, and reports on activity, resources, communities, wallets and governance, in 12 languages. Try it live at [hivescan.info](https://hivescan.info). [Repository](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/block_explorer_ui).
- **Modular dashboard** (roadmap item 1): drag-and-drop widgets, then 7 ready-made templates (Me, Network, Market, Governance, Creator, Growth and Essentials), and workspaces that sync encrypted on chain. - **Sign-in with Keychain and HiveSigner** (roadmap item 3); HiveSigner returns you to the page you came from. The signed-in menu shows upvote mana, downvote mana and RC. - **Analytics and reports** (items 4 and 6), built on haf\_stats: - activity dashboards: DAU, voting, HP distribution with a stake-concentration Lorenz curve, top accounts, retention, content volume and engagement quality; - resource and community reports: RC utilization, DApp usage, community activity and social interactions; - top holders: supply concentration (top-10 and top-100 shares, Nakamoto coefficient), labels for exchanges, the DHF and witnesses, and where you rank. - **Account Analytics (roadmap items 2 and 5):** a tab on every account page with a Financial Summary sunburst, RC footprint and DApp usage, RC consumption, content and activity, and an Influence & Delegation Map of who delegates to whom. Each report is also a dashboard widget, and most export to CSV. - **Tools hub:** Compare Accounts, a shareable account card, and a Bad Actors lookup that shows whether an account is flagged. - **Blocks page, rebuilt:** block insights, each block's mix of operation types, and a slot-health strip that shows missed slots and which witness missed them. - **Wallet and governance:** the new balances view, Total Value Locked, transfer volume, proposal vote history, incoming RC delegations, a witness missed-blocks widget, pending author and curation rewards, open orders and pending conversions, and recurring-transfer details. A fix corrected total account value, which had counted the weekly power-down twice. - **Governance tools:** a [DHF Governance Hub](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/block_explorer_ui/-/merge_requests/892) with a proposal watchlist, an impact simulator, reminders and voting straight from each proposal card, and a [Witness Dashboard](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/block_explorer_ui/-/merge_requests/895) where signed-in users see and change their witness votes. - **Quality:** 12 languages, SEO (server-side meta, sitemap, Open Graph images), link previews that now show on Telegram, Discord and X, app-wide pagination and many fixes. The explorer runs on any HAF node: where an optional app is missing, it says so instead of showing errors or empty values.
![Hivescan overview](https://usermedia.actifit.io/MVU1HUC14PEKEK7J0JIX9AB7T39OZK)
*The hivescan.info overview on 2026-10-29: live blocks, account growth, daily active users, retention funnels and HP distribution, mostly served by haf\_stats.*
### Backend apps: Balance Tracker, HAF Block Explorer, HAF, Hivemind, HiveSense, haf\_api\_node
These are the HAF backends that hivescan.info and other Hive front ends query. We added the endpoints the new dashboards needed, made slow queries fast, and fixed problems upstream where we found them, including a silent block-skip bug in Hivemind.
- **[balance\_tracker](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/balance_tracker):** - new endpoints: Total Value Locked, power-up and power-down history, RC delegations, and a top-holders balance range; - fixes: escrow tracking, which was broken for transfers, releases, approvals, disputes and fees, rebuilt with new escrow state and fee tables; routed power-downs no longer credited to the wrong account; HBD savings interest tracked per account, which the pending-interest endpoint relies on; recurrent-transfer fixes for HF28; and faster live sync. - **[haf\_block\_explorer](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_block_explorer):** - new endpoints: proposals and proposal votes with voter stake, operation-type statistics, pending HBD interest on accounts, an HBD status endpoint, a wallet-address growth endpoint (worst case from ~350 ms to under 10 ms), and a hardforks endpoint that lists HF0 to HF28 and the hardfork in force at any block; - fixes and speed: witness vote counts, which dropped lost votes and were wrong for every witness, now correct; operation-type counts read from per-block totals (about 9 ms for 1,000 blocks); a codebase restructure; and proposal-vote timeouts fixed on develop and live on testapi, shipping in the next release. - **[hivemind](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/hivemind):** a new endpoint for each user's pending author and curation rewards, with a breakdown of how each reward is calculated, and a notification wording fix. We also found a bug on our node that made Hivemind silently skip a block, diagnosed how it happens and filed it (hivemind #336); the core team traced it to a 2024 regression and fixed it. - **[hivesense](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/hivesense):** version and sync-status endpoints and a bounded retry for missing posts. Three more fixes are in review (see Upcoming work). - **[haf\_api\_node](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/haf_api_node):** haf\_stats and haf\_fyp added as standard modules, shipped in the 1.28.8 release, with gateway routes and health checks. - **Also:** a theme-aware [health checker](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive/healthchecker-component).
### GitHub (hdev-core)
Beyond GitLab, we build Hive apps in the open on GitHub under hdev-core: two front ends for haf\_fyp, a game, and four apps from our summer developer cohort that are still in development. Commit counts are for 2025-11-01 to 2026-10-28, all branches.
- **[Waggle](https://hdev-core.github.io/waggle/)**, the For You feed front end built on haf\_fyp (42 commits, mcfarhat). It offers a swipe feed, sign-in with Keychain or HiveAuth, "why this post" explanations and telemetry, voting, reblogs, follows and comments signed on-chain, and 3Speak and YouTube playback. It runs as an installable web app with no backend of its own. - **[HivePulse](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/hivepulse/hakcpohpejoejmlhiphpkjobpjeckdlg)**, a Hive browser extension and wallet for Chrome, Brave, Edge, Firefox and Firefox for Android (272 commits, mcfarhat; releases up to 1.16). From its popup, users send HIVE and HBD, claim rewards, earn HBD savings interest with an APR calculator, power up and down, delegate and manage Hive-Engine tokens, all signed through Keychain. Its Scam Shield blocks transfers and delegations to about 1,000 known scam accounts and warns on about 14,000 more. It also has a For You tab on haf\_fyp, an SEO analyzer, Ecency chat, a notification hub, an RC cost estimator and a market tab. Its weekly SEO contest pays Hive writers for posts that score well for search and AI answers: 300 to 500 HIVE in prizes each week depending on how many enter, plus referral and engagement prizes. Week 14 opened on 2026-10-27. - **[Hdev Contests](https://peakd.com/c/hive-177727)**, a Hive community we created in July 2026 to run our contests in the open. It hosts the weekly HivePulse SEO contest and the Vylor contests, and each round's rules, results and payouts are posted there. - **[Hive Runner](https://hdev-core.github.io/hive-runner/)**, a Hive-powered arcade game (Runner Dash) with Keychain login, scores posted on-chain, a live block feed, ghost racers and community teams (45 commits, mcfarhat; plus 1,387 automated leaderboard updates, not counted). It is already playable in public, ahead of its official launch. - **Summer cohort of Hive developers**: four Hive apps started over the summer and still in development, none launched yet, mentored by mcfarhat: - [Hive Freelance](https://github.com/hdev-core/hive-freelance) (140 commits), a freelance marketplace with Hive escrow; - [LINGO](https://github.com/hdev-core/lingo) (140), a daily word puzzle with an HBD reward pool; - [HiveLore](https://github.com/hdev-core/hivelore) (153), shared world-building that publishes approved stories to Hive; - [Hive Chameleon](https://github.com/hdev-core/hive-chameleon) (55), a 3D multiplayer hide-and-seek game that records match results on-chain.
### Actifit (GitHub)
[Actifit](https://actifit.io) is a move-to-earn app on Hive: users are rewarded in AFIT for logging physical activity. Actifit's own proposal, #337, ended on 2026-04-15, and its work is now covered by this one. This year brought The Arena, an on-chain challenges engine, plus a redesigned Android app, a revamped iOS app and a refreshed actifit.io: 1,473 commits in all.
- **[actifit-bot](https://github.com/actifit/actifit-bot)** (415 commits, mcfarhat): **The Arena**, a new challenges engine built on Hive. Joining, leaving and creating a challenge are signed custom\_json operations that the backend indexes from the chain. It went live in September with 6 recurring official contests, and any user can create a challenge. It has: - a challenge schema and indexer, with anti-cheat score verification; - user-created challenges, with badges or AFIT prizes split 50/30/20 among the top three; - creator-funded and recurring contests, and badges; - payouts in AFIT, and proposal-payout notifications.
Released 0.1.0 to 0.3.1. Rewards rounds also gained Hive SBI units for up to 5 winners per round. - **[actifit-landingpage](https://github.com/actifit/actifit-landingpage)** (606 commits; mcfarhat 488, reemnii 57, ShahdQaddoura 39, moamensoo 15): the [actifit.io](https://actifit.io) site, releases 1.8 to 1.14. Highlights: The Arena (create wizard, profile badges), friends, a new wallet and a revamped market (1.13), on-chain proof before web activity rewards are granted and a new signup flow (1.10), and Actifitter of the Month. - **[actifit](https://github.com/actifit/actifit)** (447 commits; mcfarhat 409, AsmaaZeid 30, Adam-Diab1 8): the Android app. - A Material Design 3 redesign, with a streak strip, a native profile screen and a signup wizard. - Health Connect integration with custom workouts and an exercise library, Fitbit step history with charts, GPS route maps, friends, an in-app DHF vote prompt, shareable "Flex" achievement cards, a configurable daily step goal and 13 languages. - Releases 0.13 "The Pump" and 0.14 "Momentum", up to 0.14.2. The Arena is now built into the app (browse, standings, join and badges) and ships in the next release. - **[iOS app](https://apps.apple.com/app/actifit-fitness-tracker/id1433969051):** public on the App Store for years. This year's 1.0.0 "Liftoff" release (August) is a complete revamp: GPS route tracking, a native profile, Snaps, Waves and Threads inside the app, a redesigned dashboard with activity rings, a social feed, an in-app AFIT market, and distance and calorie tracking from Apple Health, phone sensors and Fitbit. - **[image-hoster](https://github.com/actifit/image-hoster)** (5 commits, mcfarhat): object storage added as a third storage tier. - **Security, through the year:** in March, actifit.io began sanitizing user posts against cross-site scripting and moved its API keys behind a server-side proxy. In April and May, the backend replaced outdated and vulnerable libraries, removed unsafe handling of user input, added security tests, rate-limited login, put sensitive endpoints behind authentication and began checking on-chain proof before granting rewards. In October, a login overhaul and hack attempt prevention.
**The Actifit team:** alfamano, rabihfarhat, pjansen, katerinaramm, priyanarc, elizabethbit, silvertop and urasoul.
### Vylor
[Vylor](https://vylor.money) is a voice-first personal finance and expense-tracking app, built by mcfarhat (860 commits, private repository). It puts Hive inside an everyday money app, where users meet HIVE and HBD alongside their regular accounts. Its Hive side:
- it imports HIVE, HBD and HP balances read-only; - its PRO plan can be paid in HIVE or HBD through Keychain or HiveSigner, verified on-chain; - milestones from its Journey (XP, streaks and badges) can be posted to Hive as posts or as Waves, Snaps and Threads, signed with Keychain, HiveSigner or HiveAuth; - a Hive account counts in one live net-worth figure next to bank, crypto and brokerage accounts, with HBD valued at its $1 peg.
Vylor was built from scratch this year and launched on Hive on 2026-08-27. Beyond Hive, it has an AI voice assistant, receipt scanning, proactive alerts, a referral program, multiple accounts, CSV import, PRO reports, an Android home-screen widget, wallet portfolios across other chains, Spanish localisation and support for 44 currencies. It is live on Google Play and the App Store, at version 1.7.4. We also ran Vylor contests on Hive, in Hdev Contests: a launch contest that paid 190 HIVE and a month of Vylor PRO to its three winners, and a Talk-to-Log challenge with a $50 USDT prize.
### Public HAF API nodes we run
- **testapi.hivescan.info:** the API behind [hivescan.info](https://hivescan.info), with the full stack including haf\_stats and haf\_fyp. It was rebuilt on HAF 1.28.8 in October 2026. - **hiveapi.actifit.io:** a production 1.28.8 node that also runs a public seed (hive-seed.actifit.io).
## The team, and thanks
In all, 25 people worked on these projects this year: 4 developers on GitLab, 8 summer-cohort developers, 5 Actifit code contributors and the 8-person Actifit team. The four developers below did this year's GitLab work. A big thank you to each of them, and to everyone below who helped along the way.
| Who | Focus this year | Merged MRs | | --- | --- | --- | | mcfarhat | haf\_fyp and haf\_stats (design, build, operations), haf\_api\_node modules, HiveSense fixes, Block Explorer fixes, node operations, Waggle, HivePulse and Hive Runner, Actifit (Arena, apps, site) and Vylor | 232 | | delrifai | Block Explorer UI: dashboard, sign-in, analytics and reports, SEO, wallet and governance views | 121 | | mahdi | haf\_stats endpoints, HAF Block Explorer proposals and statistics, Balance Tracker endpoints including TVL, haf\_fyp fixes | 52 | | mzander | Balance Tracker and HAF Block Explorer backends, HAF parsers and Hivemind | 29 |
Thanks also to:
- **@blocktrades and the core team at Syncad**, and **Eric Frias (efrias)** in particular, for reviews, merges and the release work that made haf\_stats and haf\_fyp standard modules of the HAF API node stack. - **Our summer cohort of Hive developers:** lauremhsn, harfoushleen and sweidweb2 (Hive Freelance); intissarsoulaiman and laura1025 (LINGO); KareemN1936 and perlaimad (HiveLore); and mhmdibrahimm (Hive Chameleon). - **Actifit contributors:** reemnii, ShahdQaddoura and moamensoo (actifit.io), and AsmaaZeid and Adam-Diab1 (the Android app). - **Actifit socials team and moderators:** rabihfarhat, alfamano and urasoul run Actifit's socials, and our moderators keep the community going. - **louis88**, for their help with Actifit's security reviews. - **PeakD** (@asgarth), for being the first front end to serve haf\_fyp's ranking to its readers.
## Upcoming and pending work
The coming year continues our existing Hive projects and our two HAF apps, adds a new HAF app, **HAF AI**, and keeps building our other Hive projects, Actifit and Vylor. Everything in it serves one goal: bringing new users and new functionality to Hive. The plans by area follow.
### Existing Hive projects
- **Block Explorer UI ([hivescan.info](https://hivescan.info)):** grow the analytics and reports built on haf\_stats, adding dashboards as new metrics land. Extend RC as recorded cost, already shown on the account and network RC screens, to every report. Widen what signed-in users can do, building on Keychain and HiveSigner sign-in and synced workspaces. Keep the explorer current with each HAF release. - **Backend HAF apps** (Balance Tracker, HAF Block Explorer, HiveSense): new endpoints and speed-ups as the explorer and other front ends need them. Sharper HiveSense semantic search, with author and time-range filters, no deleted posts in results and safer sync checks. The author filter is already in review (hivesense !149): a search for one large author used to return nothing after 12–14 s, and for 99% of authors a search drops from ~0.4–0.75 s to ~10–25 ms. Fixes upstream where we find problems. This year, for example, we reported that any app's role could empty the HAF tables that record every app's progress (haf #348), and the core team has since closed that hole in HAF. - **Public nodes:** keep testapi.hivescan.info and hiveapi.actifit.io current with each HAF release. testapi is where our new work goes live first.
### Our HAF apps: haf\_stats and haf\_fyp
- **haf\_stats:** use each transaction's recorded RC across every report, and add network and account metrics as the explorer's reports call for them. Keep its queries fast as history grows, and keep it current in each haf\_api\_node release. - **haf\_fyp:** improve the ranking with the reading signals front ends now send: impressions, opens and dwell time. Expose the feed-freshness settings operators can now tune in the haf\_api\_node configuration, and make sure front ends' telemetry passes the node gateway. Bring the feed to more front ends, Denser included, and keep it current in the standard release.
### New: HAF AI
HAF AI is an MCP server that gives AI agents (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and others) citable, fresh access to Hive data that HAF nodes already serve. That covers HiveSense search, Hivemind posts and communities, HAfAH account history, haf\_stats metrics and haf\_fyp's ranked feed. Every answer links back to Hive, which turns AI answers into a way into Hive. It is read-only, holds no keys and runs no language model of its own.
1. **Pilot:** 7 tools on testapi.hivescan.info, with one real user through a Claude connector (about 3 weeks). 2. **Public listing:** account and community tools, metrics, the ranked feed, a haf\_api\_node module and a citation resolver (about 8 more weeks). This phase needs reviews from HiveSense and haf\_api\_node maintainers, one front end, and a second node operator. 3. **After listing:** topic briefs, onboarding answers and an agent-disclosure standard. 4. **Intelligence:** a curation score that resists gaming, profiles and topic tools, built with the HiveSense maintainers.
Success target, 90 days after listing: 500 citation click-throughs a week, and 40 distinct callers a week with 15 of them returning. If it falls short (fewer than 5 returning callers, or fewer than 100 click-throughs a week), we reassess before building further.
### Other Hive projects on GitHub
- **Waggle:** keep it as the reference front end for haf\_fyp, picking up new ranking features as they land and extending its "why this post" explanations. - **HivePulse:** keep improving the extension, its wallet, Scam Shield, For You tab and SEO analyzer, and keep running its weekly contests. - **Hive Runner:** take the game from public preview to launch, with its live block feed and on-chain scores. - **The summer cohort's apps** (Hive Freelance, LINGO, HiveLore, Hive Chameleon): take them from development to a public launch on Hive.
### Actifit
- **The Arena:** more challenge types and contests on the on-chain challenges engine launched this year, building on its AFIT prizes and badges, and release it in the Android app. - **Apps and site:** keep improving the Android and iOS apps, and grow actifit.io alongside them.
### Vylor
- Deepen its Hive integration. Planned items include HBD savings and transfers by voice, an on-chain backup and habit rewards.
## Proposal ask
We are requesting **275 HBD/day** from 2026-12-01 to 2027-12-31, **about 34% less** than the adjusted rate of our recent proposal, [#360](https://peakd.com/proposals/360).
Actifit's own proposal, #337, ended on 2026-04-15, and the team has not filed another since. Its work is covered by this one, so the DHF now funds one proposal from us instead of two.
Proposal #2 was funded for only about half its term, yet the year's work went on: 434 merged MRs, two new HAF apps in the standard node release, and the Block Explorer's analytics hub.
Given the state of crypto prices, we cut our own costs before setting the ask. We have reduced the developer time this proposal pays for, and cut our infrastructure: last year we ran more API nodes and servers, and we now run only the two public HAF API nodes named above. The ask splits roughly as follows, based on last year's spending:
| Area | Share | HBD/day (approx.) | | --- | --- | --- | | Development | 77% | 210 | | Outreach and growth (socials, marketing and contest payouts) | 18% | 51 | | Infrastructure | 5% | 14 |
## How to follow our work
We post regular progress updates on Hive, and all our work is open source: the HAF apps and the Block Explorer on [GitLab](https://gitlab.syncad.com/hive), and our other apps on GitHub ([hdev-core](https://github.com/hdev-core), [Actifit](https://github.com/actifit)). Every item in this proposal links to a merge request or a live endpoint, so anyone can check our progress at any time, and withdraw their vote if we fall short.
## Support this proposal (391)
We invite you to support our third proposal and help us keep building Hive's open-source tools and bringing new users to Hive.
- [Vote on PeakD](https://peakd.com/me/proposals/391) - [Vote on Ecency](https://ecency.com/proposals/391) - [Vote on the Hive wallet](https://wallet.hive.blog/proposals) - [Vote via HiveSigner](https://hivesigner.com/sign/update_proposal_votes?proposal_ids=%5B%22391%22%5D&approve=true)
Thank you for your continued support.

entry.content:
![3Speak dev update, October 21 to 27, 2026](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRj62mF3en5JzJe277aYdPVWHQ3TSn97e89iL81ZaTf6G/thumbnail.png) **The short version** - **24-hour Stories** are live for everyone: post your own, and watch them on the home page and first in the Shorts feed. - A new **leaderboard** for Videos, Shorts, Stories and Tags, and a **Customize profile** editor. - Comments got sorting, creator pins, images and a preview tab. - **Supporters**: every tip on a video is now recorded and shown. - Reshare is now called **Hype**, and there is a real Hive **Reblog** button next to it. - Hive-style addresses like `3speak.tv/@yourname`, and a preview image for every shared link. - Faster home feeds, fewer stalls when a Hive node goes down, and much better visibility on Google and Bing. - Ads play quieter, fill portrait videos properly and adapt to slow connections. - Under the hood: hot storage node fixes, a smarter encoder and a new Snapie release. --- ## 🌐 3speak.tv website [new-3speak-tv](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv) · 9 releases, all live
### 24-hour Stories are here
![A 24-hour story playing on 3Speak](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTMrRJ8EvGPjtpbHD6ZUZZwNzQLSVKDrKWCtzWHeiqu5C/stories-live.png)
**Stories** are short videos that disappear after 24 hours. They lead the [home page](https://3speak.tv) in a row with a countdown ring, come first in the [Shorts feed](https://3speak.tv/shorts) with a "time left" badge, and your followers get a notification when you post one. They are open to everyone: anyone with a Hive account can post a story, and everyone can watch them. - **Two taps to post** a story. - **Seen by:** see who watched your story. - **Keep as short:** turn a story into a normal short before it runs out. - **Streaks:** count the days in a row you posted a story, with its own spot on the [leaderboard](https://3speak.tv/leaderboard). ![Stories lead the 3Speak home page](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPkpU8nzGJnEo7M3YgSNDLX6pFXnDuqvT7mjfaWW12FHr/stories-row.png) ([#534](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/534))
### A leaderboard for every kind of video
![The new 3Speak leaderboard](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbrQFK7798ListQ2UamzkkDWQcTaQELefaxBchY1YKTK7/leaderboard.png)
The [leaderboard](https://3speak.tv/leaderboard) now has chips for Videos, Shorts, Stories and Tags. Rank creators by watch time or by count, and pick the time range right in the header: 7 days, 30 days, a year or all time. ([#534](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/534))
### Customize your profile
![The profile layout editor on 3Speak](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNzeFBimJqKduB8mafJAQUyYWAmFNfGQ67iBWtev18aiH/profile-editor.png)
On your own profile, **Customize profile** lets you drag the Overview sections into the order you like, resize them, hide the ones you don't need and set up a separate layout for phones. Nothing changes for your visitors until you press Save. ([#534](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/534))
### Titles for Shorts [Shorts](https://3speak.tv/shorts) can now carry a title, set when you upload or edit them. ([#534](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/534))
### Remix chains share the rewards A remix of a remix used to pay and credit only the video it came from directly. Now every earlier creator in the chain, up to six videos back, gets a share of the rewards and a link in the post. ([#534](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/534))
### Comments: sort, pin, add images, preview
![The new comment tools on a 3Speak watch page](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbqa6ce976udUEkMM84ccxvPCbVCbwRvLVz8PyQogrk58/comments.png)
Comments on [videos](https://3speak.tv/@enraizar/richard-avedon-in-the-ameri-475) and [Shorts](https://3speak.tv/shorts) can now be sorted, and creators can pin up to three comments to the top of their video. You can add images to a comment, and a Write / Preview tab shows how it will look before you send it. ([#525](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/525))
### Supporters: every tip counts
![The Supporters tab on a 3Speak profile](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeGvW6AXkYaHfsny5cekGesW6cY359A3NK1rkE2LKmXzT/supporters.png)
Every tip sent to a video's creator is now recorded, after checking the real transfer on Hive, so nobody can fake one. Profiles show tips received and given, and a [Supporters tab](https://3speak.tv/@enraizar?tab=supporters) lists who supported whom, with their memos. A tip can also be hidden, and tip memos now link to the video or audio post you tipped. ([#525](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/525), [#534](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/534))
### Hype, and a real Hive Reblog
![Hype and Reblog buttons on the watch page](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXUrqHog5MVRyndownb9jdnBKbGfsXozCperTGy5WKabE/hype-reblog.png)
Many people took our "Reshare" button for a Hive reblog. It isn't one, so it is now called **Hype** and has a flame icon. Next to it there is now a real **Reblog** button that reblogs the post on Hive, on the [watch page](https://3speak.tv/@enraizar/richard-avedon-in-the-ameri-475) and the post page. It asks for a second tap to confirm, and doesn't show on your own posts. ([#529](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/529))
### "For Hive post" in the share menu
![The share menu with the new For Hive post option](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZYjquB22n1tGigU37ACRBFTKwoGvCK4w1YW52m9wN5Ss/share-menu.png)
The [share menu](https://3speak.tv/@enraizar/richard-avedon-in-the-ameri-475) on the watch page has a new option that copies the classic `3speak.tv/watch?v=` link, the one that works in every Hive frontend when you put it in a post. ([#529](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/529))
### Autoplay you can stop Before the next video starts you now see a 3, 2, 1 countdown you can cancel, and it waits while you're away from the player. Autoplay also no longer skips past a video that is still processing: it checks again every 20 seconds and plays it once it's ready. ([#524](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/524), [#525](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/525))
### Hive-style addresses: /@user and /@author/permlink
![A 3Speak profile at its new /@ address](https://images.hive.blog/DQmT9nwp6zNdS3BVKTayK7ynhSmRJW5TD39Wvuf1vNzk15C/profile-address.png)
Profiles and videos now live at the same kind of address you know from other Hive apps. Take a Hive link, swap the domain for 3speak.tv, and you land on the same [profile](https://3speak.tv/@enraizar) or [video](https://3speak.tv/@enraizar/richard-avedon-in-the-ameri-475). Your old links still work: `/user/...`, `/p/...` and `/watch?v=...` open the same page and move you to the new address. Links that 3Speak writes into your Hive posts stay as `watch?v=`, so they keep working everywhere. ([#532](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/532))
### A preview image for every link you share
![Share card of the Threespeak community](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSeUuMpgv7J5L9twJrMfv9Vhu3yxnog29RDVLWJq34vQB/share-card.png)
Paste a 3Speak link into Discord, Telegram, X or a chat app and you get a picture card instead of a bare link. Every channel and every [Hive community](https://3speak.tv/communities) now has its own card with its picture and name, and tags, [badges](https://3speak.tv/badges), playlists, [audio posts](https://3speak.tv/audio), invite links and the main feeds got cards too. The homepage got a proper wide banner instead of a stretched square logo. ([#529](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/529), [#532](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/532))
### Easier to find on Google and Bing Search engines used to see only about 3,600 of our videos. Now: - the [sitemap](https://3speak.tv/sitemap.xml) lists about **123,000 videos and shorts**, and every channel with a video (about 6,500, up from 249) - every watch page tells search engines it holds a video, with the player, chapters and links to the channel and tags, so videos can appear in video search results - each page has one clear address, and pages that don't exist answer with a real "not found" - new uploads are announced to Bing and the other IndexNow search engines every 10 minutes The same work fixed a slow network lookup that had stopped Discord from showing inline video previews. ([#530](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/530))
### Shared playlist links open the playlist When someone sends you a link to a video inside a playlist, you now get the playlist bar next to the video, the same as when you click through the playlist yourself. Private playlists stay private. ([#533](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/533))
### Smaller fixes - **[Discover](https://3speak.tv/discover) Spotlight** no longer disappears when you hide AI videos. It now just skips the AI-flagged ones. - [Discover](https://3speak.tv/discover) shows one community snap per creator, so one busy account can't fill the row. - Members-only videos now say "Members". - The share menu got wider rows with short descriptions and a Playlist shortcut, and opens as a sheet from the bottom on phones. - [Discover](https://3speak.tv/discover) Spotlight loads sooner and keeps its place while it loads. - Thumbnails stored on IPFS load again, through 3Speak's own gateway. - Warm-up videos: the Follow feed shows only warm-up creators you follow, and [New](https://3speak.tv/new) places their videos by date. - Switching between Butter Auth and a Hive wallet login now asks whether to reuse or replace the wallet login. - Calmer buttons, and one consistent header on every pop-up. - Spotlight link icons show the right logo again (Dropbox and Netflix links had been getting the X icon), plus a few other bugs our new test suite caught. - A round of security fixes for the site's API. - Warm-up accounts get a clear message, in all 21 languages, when they try to post the same comment twice. ([#525](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/525), [#527](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/527), [#531](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/531), [#532](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/532), [#534](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/534))
### For developers The site's code got unit, API and browser test suites, a rewritten README, contributing docs and an MIT license. ([#527](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/new-3speak-tv/pull/527)) --- ## ⚡ Feeds and API [3speakchecks](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks) · 12 changes The "checker" is the service behind 3Speak's feeds, ads, the [leaderboard](https://3speak.tv/leaderboard) and many other features. It also got the server side of comment pins and Supporters ([#80](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/80)).
### Home feeds load faster
![Feed load times before and after](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbo3vXTkw5oByzpnJWYa34C3sTJLi85vpzS1pSEZxjtMj/feeds.png)
[Trending](https://3speak.tv/trend), [New](https://3speak.tv/new) and [Shorts](https://3speak.tv/shorts) used to rebuild the same list of candidate videos for every visitor, waiting on the database and on Hive each time. Now that list is built once, kept fresh in the background and shared. Your personal touches (creators you follow, your interests, hidden and watched videos) are still applied on every visit. The trade-off: a brand new upload can take a minute or two longer to show up in these three feeds. ([#82](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/82))
### No more 10-second waits when a Hive node is down When a Hive API node stops answering, the checker now moves on after 3 seconds instead of 10, and lets that node sit out for a minute while the next one takes over. On October 25 one node failed 135 times in a day. In a test with a dead node first in line, the first request took 3.4 seconds and the ones after it less than 0.1 seconds. ([#83](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/83))
### Ads that fit the video ![Ad changes before and after](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZtNkp4kgdzHUWByYiKNQ4KzYVVrbqU9BEVWDHLEGvtmN/ads.png) - **Quieter.** Every ad now plays 2 dB below its original level, the same on every playback. - **Landscape ads fill portrait videos.** A landscape ad inside a portrait video used to play as a tiny letterboxed picture (268x151 pixels in one real case). It now plays as a proper landscape video that fills the player. - **Ads between [Shorts](https://3speak.tv/shorts) adapt to your connection.** They used to play only in 1080p and could stall on a phone. Now they start near 720p and adapt like any other video. ([#76](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/76), [#78](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/78))
### Warm-up posts Warm-up accounts are new people trying 3Speak before they have their own Hive account. Their posts get a few slots in [Discover](https://3speak.tv/discover). - **More variety:** one very active account was filling most of those slots, so each account now gets at most one post per load. ([#81](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/81)) - **No doubles:** people who already made their own Hive account under their warm-up name no longer show up twice. ([#79](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/79)) - **Announcements arrive:** personal announcements sent to a warm-up user by name now reach them. ([#84](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/84))
### 24-hour Stories, behind the scenes The checker does the server side of Stories, live since this week's release: - a Stories row with the creators you follow first, and a "seen" state - live stories lead the [shorts feed](https://3speak.tv/shorts) and disappear everywhere once they expire - **Keep as short**: turn a story into a normal short before it runs out - **Seen by**: see who watched your story - **Streaks**: the number of days in a row you posted a story - two new [leaderboard](https://3speak.tv/leaderboard) metrics, story uploads and story streak ([#85](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/85), [#86](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/86), [#87](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/87), [#88](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakchecks/pull/88)) --- ## ▶️ Video player [snapievideoplayer](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapievideoplayer) · 3 changes ![The expired-story screen in the player](https://images.hive.blog/DQmdwCCaMo1zjUqAgjf3Cw7ognjC2279xEojpRA7nmQAmdF/story.png) - **No ads on notice videos.** When a video is still processing, deleted or failed, the player shows a short notice instead. Ads no longer play on top of those, so [advertisers](https://3speak.tv/advertise) don't pay for an empty view. ([#51](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapievideoplayer/pull/51)) - **Portrait stays portrait.** A landscape ad at the start of a portrait video no longer makes the player treat the whole video as landscape. ([#52](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapievideoplayer/pull/52)) - **Expired stories.** Once a story's 24 hours are up, the player shows a short "This story has expired" clip instead, in embeds too. On 3speak.tv an expired story already gets its own screen; embeds get this clip with the next player update. ([#53](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapievideoplayer/pull/53)) --- ## 🎞️ Encoder [3speakencoder](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder) · 1 change Some uploads are small in resolution but huge in file size, like a 480p video of about 700 MB. The encoder used to pass those through untouched. Now it only skips re-encoding when a video is already at or below the normal size for its resolution, so oversized uploads get brought down to the usual quality settings like every other video. ([#39](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speakencoder/pull/39)) --- ## 🤖 AI check and leaderboard jobs [3speak-subtitle-generator](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-subtitle-generator) · 1 change This project runs background jobs for 3Speak, including the AI-content check and the [leaderboard](https://3speak.tv/leaderboard) numbers. - Leaderboard numbers for Stories: story uploads and story streaks. - The AI-content check now also covers videos from warm-up accounts. - A video with broken or unusual details no longer stops a whole batch. - Copying video files to the storage nodes is more reliable. ([#2](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-subtitle-generator/pull/2)) --- ## ✂️ Video editor [3speak-editor-suite](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite) · 5 changes The editor opens when you [upload](https://3speak.tv/upload) a Short or make a remix on 3speak.tv. Its code is now public on GitHub. ![The editor's sound fixes, before and after](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQuXM3VQ3TB7i8RFsVb4R9bbnL8vP6WCVsn2L5jps9EvD/editor-audio.png) - **Teleprompter follows your voice in any browser.** "Follow voice" used to work only in Chrome-based browsers. It now works in Firefox and others too. ([#7](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/7)) - **Volume 0 means silent.** A clip set to volume 0 used to play and render at full volume. Muted tracks, hidden tracks and clips with sound turned off now stay out of the final video, just like in the preview. ([#8](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/8)) - **The mix sounds like the preview.** With music and several clips together, the final video came out much quieter than the preview (four sources each played at a quarter). Each source now keeps its own volume. ([#8](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/8)) - **Remixing never touches your draft.** Opening a remix used to ask "Replace your saved draft?". Remixes no longer autosave, so your saved draft stays exactly as it was. ([#13](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/13)) - **Cropped overlays render like the preview.** In a camera-overlay remix, a freely placed and cropped clip came out zoomed and shifted in the final video. It now lands where the preview shows it. ([#14](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/14)) - **Sign-in to upload and render.** Uploading and rendering in the editor now needs a 3Speak sign-in. ([#10](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/3speak-editor-suite/pull/10)) --- ## 💾 Hot storage node [hotnode](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/hotnode) · 6 changes ![Hot node pin lookups before and after](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRQLTSnxE5xujFDzWvoJA6t13o2xHLnZYjqaFf785xRqC/hotnode.png) The hot node keeps fresh uploads on fast IPFS storage so they start quickly, before they move to long-term storage. - **Popular videos stay on fast storage.** A video used to leave the hot node as soon as it was old enough and copied to long-term storage. Now it also has to go quiet: a video watched in the last 7 days keeps its place, however old it is. ([#2](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/hotnode/pull/2)) - **No more crashes while finding new videos.** Each lookup loaded about 150,000 video records into memory and ran out of it. It now asks the database for just the one it needs. ([#6](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/hotnode/pull/6)) - **Fewer false "copy failed" errors.** Checking that a video arrived on long-term storage now gets 2 minutes instead of 30 seconds, because that node can be slow under load. ([#1](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/hotnode/pull/1)) - **Deploys itself.** Once set up on the server, a merge goes live within about two minutes, and a failed deploy rolls back on its own. ([#5](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/hotnode/pull/5)) - **A stats page you can trust.** Fixed daily counters that reset to empty, migration sizes that always read 0, freed storage that was counted twice, and CPU numbers that showed 0% most of the time. ([#9](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/hotnode/pull/9), [#10](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/hotnode/pull/10)) --- ## 📱 Snapie [snapie-io](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapie-io) · 1 release · live on [snapie.io](https://snapie.io) - **Games:** floating touch controls for Rush, Puff Quest and Blocks, and Blocks fits fullscreen. Jump's title no longer overlaps in landscape. - **Feed:** when your mute list hides most of a page, the feed keeps loading instead of looking stuck. - **Images:** a missing Hivemoji no longer shows up as a server error. - **Composer:** the emoji picker no longer covers the Post button. ([#313](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/snapie-io/pull/313)) --- ## 🚦 Traffic director [trafficdirector](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/trafficdirector) · 1 change Cleanup: an unused example endpoint is gone, so there is less code facing the internet. ([#2](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft/trafficdirector/pull/2)) --- That's it for this week. Most of our code is open on GitHub at [github.com/Mantequilla-Soft](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft). Questions, bug reports or ideas? Drop them in the comments below.
[![Mantequilla Soft](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSCTXSSRQ4R5Xq2pGTTiiMuSsTcJYAy1ozfkb35M7jVzB/mantequilla-soft-logo.png)](https://www.mantequilla-soft.com) **[GitHub](https://github.com/Mantequilla-Soft) · [Website](https://www.mantequilla-soft.com) · [Snapie](https://snapie.io) · [3Speak](https://3speak.tv)**
Source: 3Speak: Your Profile, Your Stories, Your Supporters by @mantequilla-soft
